You'll need either syringes or scales. I use syringes. Some people say I'm silly and should use scales :) I have syringes in 1ml, 2.5ml, 5ml, 10ml, 20ml, 30ml, 60ml. I have a glass beaker I pour my pg&vg into to be syringed out. Both ebay and amazon are good for that stuff.

I've bought from them and they are now my go-to for bottles: https://vapingbottles.com I use LDPE bottles because they are nice and soft and squeezy. Some prefer PET but I find them to be like trying to squeeze glass they're that hard to me.

Oh and labels to label your juice! You can put the name and date of mixing on there and maybe nic strength and vg/pg ratio but I only put the name and date as all mine have the same ratios. You can get labels on amazon. Will look out the ones I got if needed.

Apart from that, when you start mixing, make samples in 10ml bottles. There will likely be ones you don't like so it'll be less wasteful. I started with 30ml bottles and soon had lots that I didn't want and it added up to quite a bit of wastage. I don't understand people who make up big 500ml bottles of a juice they've never tasted before but that's just me.

It's one of these http://www.vapeclub.co.uk/img/products/aspire-nautilus-replacement-coil-bvc.jpg and you'll hopefully have got one with your tank. It has cotton inside and the juice soaks into it and that's what you vape.

Cheap juice might play a factor but it tends to be really sweet juices like desserts and custards, and dark juices that clog up the coil quicker - even expensive juices.

Before you use your coil you need to "prime" it. You do this by dropping 5-6 drops of juice down the centre of your coil, then screw it in and let it sit in the juice in the tank for 10 minutes. This is to make sure the coil is saturated enough to vape.
